governing_intent: Implement the first canonical Python package skeleton for AlienIntent under the Founder-fixed src/alienintent layout while preserving the existing Node bootstrap unchanged, and add executable architecture fitness checks that prove the intended structural boundaries before any runtime capability is introduced.
summary: The proposed work has a clear bounded outcome: create the approved Python repository/package structure, add enforceable architecture fitness checks, demonstrate those checks failing on deliberate violations and passing on the skeleton, retain evidence, and verify Node still coexists unchanged. The supplied text states the relevant architecture authority, fixed layout, exclusions, and acceptance criteria, with no unresolved Founder-level decisions remaining.
implementation_unknowns: Exact contents and formatting of docs/work-units/python/PY-01.md are not independently verified here and must be followed by the implementation agent if available in the repository.
The implementation mechanism for the fitness checks remains an engineering choice: for example AST inspection, import graph analysis, custom pytest checks, or another local executable checker.

The precise definition of 'vendor types in domain or port signatures' must be encoded conservatively from existing repository conventions and approved architecture language without inventing new product contracts.
The method for preserving evidence, including filenames, location, and captured exit statuses, is an implementation detail unless the BIU specifies it.
The existing Node test command and Python test/build commands must be discovered from repository tooling rather than assumed.
verification_assessment: Acceptance is observable through filesystem layout checks, executable architecture fitness checks with intentional failing fixtures and passing skeleton cases, preserved command outputs or logs showing real exit statuses, and a Node suite run demonstrating the bootstrap remains unchanged. One independent verification verdict is meaningful because the work is a cohesive structural/conformance vertical with explicit exclusions and no runtime behavior to validate beyond coexistence and boundary enforcement.
material_risks: Fitness checks may accidentally overreach by enforcing contracts or bounded contexts not required for this step, which would consume excluded design work.
Fitness checks may be too weak or fixture-specific if they only detect the deliberate violations and do not generalize to real future code.
Creating or editing pyproject.toml could affect repository packaging or tooling if the existing project already has Node-oriented assumptions; changes must remain compatible with Node coexistence.

Node must remain operationally authoritative and untouched except for unavoidable coexistence-neutral repository metadata; accidental Node source, test, runtime, or bootstrap edits would violate scope.
Evidence retention must include real executable outcomes rather than static descriptions, or the EOS requirement for executable proof would not be met.
next_action: Hand off for implementation of PY-01 exactly within the fixed Python skeleton, tools/fitness, tests, and evidence scope; discover existing commands locally, add the minimum executable checks and fixtures, run the relevant Python checks and Node suite, preserve real outputs, and avoid all Node source/runtime/config changes.
rationale: READY is the controlling disposition because the owner intent, architecture authority, repository layout, exclusions, and acceptance criteria are specific and coherent. Remaining uncertainties are normal engineering research about how to implement and run the checks, not unresolved owner decisions. The work is one cohesive vertical: the skeleton and fitness checks mutually validate the same architectural boundary baseline, so splitting would add coordination overhead without isolating independent product decisions. No external prerequisite is established as unavailable by the supplied text.
